9.text: In currying reindeer-skins the Chukchee women do not manifest much

10.text: skill. This work is neglected because the curried leather is comparatively

11.text: little used among the Chukchee. For currying, the skin is soaked and left

12.text: for twenty-four hours folded together. Then the hair is scraped off and the

13.text: skin is dried. Such scraped skins are brought by the Chukchee to every fair,

14.text: because they are much lighter than those with the hair on. In the further

15.text: process of preparing the skin, it is smeared with any one of the materials

16.text: mentioned above, then scraped again, and bleached in the wind or dyed with

17.text: yellow ochre. The Russianized natives even wash the finest curried skins with

18.text: soap, and then dry them in the air, giving them a snow-white appearance.
